title: Clear sight versus a life where wrong looks beautiful.
subtitle: The two people are not equal
then: Ibn Kathir describes the first person as {idea}on clear vision and certainty, through the Book and the pure nature Allah created him with.{/idea} The second has {trap}his bad deeds made to look beautiful, and follows his own lusts.{/trap} The two can never be equal.
now: A habit you know is wrong starts to look normal, even attractive, because everyone posts it. {trap}That is what made attractive feels like from the inside.{/trap} {idea}Clear evidence from your Lord is what lets you see it as it is.{/idea}
old: If something looks good and feels normal, it probably is fine.
new: Wrong can be made to look beautiful, so I need guidance to see clearly.
try: Name one thing that has started to look normal to you. Hold it up against one verse.

title: Four rivers that never spoil, and forgiveness on top.
subtitle: The description of Paradise promised to the mindful
then: Ibn Kathir says the water does not change or smell, the milk is pure and rich, the wine has no bad effect, and the honey is perfectly pure. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}when you ask Allah, ask for al-Firdaws, the highest part, from which the rivers flow.{/reward} {idea}Above all of it is forgiveness from their Lord.{/idea}
now: Milk in your fridge goes off in a week. Your favorite treat gives you a stomachache. Everything here spoils a little. {reward}The verse describes good things that do not turn.{/reward} {idea}And it crowns them with forgiveness, the thing you most need.{/idea}
old: Every pleasure has a downside, so nothing can be fully good.
new: Allah has prepared good things that do not spoil, and forgiveness above them.
try: In your dua today, ask Allah by name for al-Firdaws.

title: Sitting in the gathering, then asking what was just said.
subtitle: Present in body, absent in heart
then: Ibn Kathir describes hypocrites who sat with the Prophet ﷺ and listened {trap}without understanding anything, nor caring.{/trap} Afterwards they asked the Companions what he had just said. {trap}Their hearts were sealed because they followed their desires.{/trap}
now: You sat through the whole Friday sermon. In the car someone asks what it was about, and you have no idea. You were planning your week. {idea}Being in the room is not the same as hearing.{/idea}
old: Showing up is the main thing.
new: Showing up matters, but my heart has to be there too to take anything away.
try: At the next talk or reminder you hear, write down one sentence from it afterwards.

title: Take one step toward guidance and more is given.
subtitle: Guidance grows for those who accept it
then: After the sealed hearts comes the opposite. Ibn Kathir says {reward}those who seek guidance, Allah makes it easy for them, guides them to it, makes them firm on it, and gives them more.{/reward} {idea}He also inspires them with their taqwa.{/idea}
now: You started with one short surah after Fajr. A month later you want to know what it means. Then you want to live it. {reward}That growth is the increase this verse promises.{/reward}
old: Guidance is something some people just have and others do not.
new: When I move toward guidance, Allah gives me more of it.
try: Take one small step toward learning your faith today: one verse, one meaning.

title: Waiting for the Hour, while its signs have already come.
subtitle: Remembering then will not help
then: Ibn Kathir says the coming of the Prophet ﷺ is itself one of the signs of the Hour, because he is the last Messenger ﷺ. Sahl bin Sa'd saw him join his index and middle fingers and say {idea}I have been sent before the Hour like these two.{/idea} {trap}When it comes, remembering will not help.{/trap}
now: You keep saying you will get serious about prayer after this busy month, after the wedding, after retirement. {trap}The verse says do not wait for a sudden ending to start remembering.{/trap} {idea}The signs are already here.{/idea}
old: There is plenty of time; I will get serious later.
new: The signs have already come, and remembering is only useful before the end.
try: Pick one thing you keep postponing for later in your faith and do a piece of it today.

title: Know there is no god but Allah, then ask forgiveness.
subtitle: Knowledge first, then forgiveness for you and others

row.title: everyone
sub: the Prophet ﷺ, 70 times a day

then: The command begins with knowing that there is no god but Allah. Then it joins that to seeking forgiveness for oneself and for all believers. Ibn Kathir records that the Prophet ﷺ said {idea}I ask Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him more than seventy times every day.{/idea} {reward}Allah knows your moving about and your place of rest.{/reward}
now: You make dua only for yourself and your family. {reward}This verse widens it: every believing man and woman.{/reward} The stranger on the bus, the doctor on night shift, the person who annoyed you in the queue.
old: Asking forgiveness is for when I have done something bad.
new: Seeking forgiveness is a daily habit, for me and for every believer.
try: Say astaghfirullah for yourself and for all believing men and women ten times today.

title: Asking for a hard command, then fainting when it comes.
subtitle: The gap between wishing and doing
then: The surah introduction says Madinah was tiny and surrounded. Ibn Kathir says believers hoped for a surah ordering them to fight. {trap}When it came, those with sickness in their hearts looked at the Prophet ﷺ like someone fainting at death.{/trap} {idea}The verse compares it to those who asked, then wanted it postponed.{/idea}
now: You say you would give anything for your parents. Then your mother needs a lift to the hospital at 6am and you groan. {trap}The wish was easy; the real ask shows where you are.{/trap}
old: I know I would do the hard thing if it were ever asked of me.
new: The test is not what I wish for but how I respond when it actually arrives.
try: Do one thing today you once said you would gladly do, now that it is actually asked.

title: Obedience and a good word would have been better.
subtitle: Being true when it becomes serious

key.label: What helps in a hard moment

then: After the fearful look comes gentle advice. Ibn Kathir says {idea}it would have been better for them to listen and obey in that situation.{/idea} When the matter became serious, {reward}being sincere to Allah would have been better for them.{/reward}
now: The family emergency, the hard diagnosis, the redundancy letter. You want to panic and complain to everyone. {idea}The verse offers a calmer path: obey, speak well, be sincere.{/idea} {reward}It is better for you, not only for Allah's cause.{/reward}
old: When things get serious, panic and complaint are only natural.
new: In serious moments, quiet obedience and good words serve me best.
try: The next time stress hits today, choose one good sentence to say instead of a complaint.

title: Turn away, and you go back to corruption and cutting family.
subtitle: What turning away really brings
then: Ibn Kathir says turning away would mean returning to the old ways of ignorance: bloodshed and cutting off relatives. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: {reward}the womb sought refuge in Allah from being cut, and Allah promised to join whoever joins it.{/reward} {idea}Joining ties is not dealing evenly, but reaching those who cut you off.{/idea}
now: There is an aunt you have not called in two years because she did not call you. A cousin muted in the family chat. {idea}Keeping score feels fair.{/idea} {reward}The verse and the hadith ask you to reach out first.{/reward}
old: I will keep in touch with relatives who keep in touch with me.
new: Keeping family ties means reaching out even to those who do not reach back.
try: Send one kind message today to a relative you have drifted away from.

title: Those who do this lose their hearing and their sight.
subtitle: Cutting ties dulls the heart
then: Ibn Kathir says this involves a general ban on spreading corruption and a specific one on cutting family ties. He cites the Prophet ﷺ: {trap}no sin more deserves to have its punishment hastened in this world than injustice and cutting kinship.{/trap} {reward}And whoever wants a longer life and more provision should join his ties.{/reward}
now: The family feud has gone on so long nobody remembers how it started. Everyone just avoids the other side at weddings. {idea}The verse says this is not small.{/idea} {reward}Mending it can open blessings you have not seen.{/reward}
old: A family feud is private and does not affect my faith.
new: Cutting off family is serious before Allah, and joining it brings real blessing.
try: Make dua tonight for one relative you are distant from, by name.

title: Do they not reflect, or are their hearts locked?
subtitle: The Quran is meant to be thought about
then: Ibn Kathir reports that when the Prophet ﷺ recited this, a young man from Yemen said {reward}there are locks on them, until Allah opens them, fully or a little.{/reward} Umar liked him for this and later made him an adviser. {idea}The verse commands reflection, not just recitation.{/idea}
now: You can finish a whole juz on your commute and not remember a single meaning. {idea}Speed is not the goal.{/idea} {reward}One verse you actually think about can open the lock a little.{/reward}
old: Reading more pages is the main way to benefit from the Quran.
new: Reflecting on even one verse matters more than racing through pages.
try: Read one verse slowly today, then sit for one minute with what it asks of you.

title: Turning back after it was clear, sold on false hopes.
subtitle: How Shaytan pulls someone away
then: This is about those who left faith after guidance had become clear. Ibn Kathir says Shaytan {trap}adorned it for them and filled them with false hopes, tempting and deceiving them.{/trap}
now: You drift from prayer slowly. A voice says: you are young, there is time, everyone does it, you will come back. {trap}That is the long false hope.{/trap} {idea}Notice the voice, and do not let it set your timetable.{/idea}
old: I have plenty of time to get back on track.
new: The feeling that there is always more time is one of Shaytan's oldest tools.
try: If you have been drifting, pray the next prayer on time, today, not later.

title: We will obey you in part, said in secret.
subtitle: Half-loyalty to those who hate the truth
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}plotted secretly with those who hated revelation and gave them evil advice{/trap}, as hypocrites show one thing and hide another. {idea}Allah knows whatever they hide.{/idea}
now: In one group chat you say all the right things. In another, you mock the same values to fit in. {trap}Just partly going along.{/trap} {idea}Allah sees both chats.{/idea}
old: What I say in private does not really count.
new: Allah knows my private words as clearly as my public ones.
try: Notice one place where you speak differently about your faith to fit in. Speak once as yourself.
